| identity | `required-open` | A token is one of the twenty-five kinds of the standard's list, with what the standard says each carries. A value of code points is a list of characters, and a numeric value is a rational number. A component value, a declaration and a rule are the results of parsing as the standard names them. One tree is written and read. Open: no declaration record names each declaration's owner and the anchor of the algorithm it models; the docstrings name the heading identifiers of the sealed source. Discharged: declarations `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.Token`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.Numeric`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.Component`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.Declaration`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.Rule` and `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.Stylesheet`. |
| construction | `required-open` | A writer builds a list of tokens and asks whether it is writable: each token is one the tokenizer can give and the writer can write, and three kinds say what must follow them. Open: not every value of `Token` is one the tokenizer gives: `Writable` is a test and not a type, and a caller that builds tokens by hand holds no proof until it runs the test. Discharged: declarations `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.Token.ofIdent`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.Token.writable` and `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.Writable`. |
| semantics | `required-open` | `consumeToken` is the standard's `consume a token`, with one function for each algorithm it calls, each named after its heading in the sealed source. `tokenize` repeats it to the end of the input. Every token takes at least one code point, which is how `tokenize` ends. Open: parse errors are comments at their place and not values: the model returns the tokens the standard says are returned, and says nothing of which inputs are errors; the parser of the standard, from tokens to rules, is not modelled (slice K4); decoding bytes to code points is not modelled: the input is a list of code points, after the standard's preprocessing (`filterCodePoints`). Discharged: declarations `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.tokenize`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.tokenizeText`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.consumeToken` and `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.filterCodePoints`; theorems `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.consumeToken_length_lt`. |
| laws | `required-open` | Tokenizing what the writer wrote gives the tokens back, with each run of white space as one, for every writable list. It is built from one law for each kind of token (the text of a token before a text that stops it reads as the token and then that text) and from the table of pairs, cell by cell (the next token's text stops the one before, where no comment is put). Open: the round trip is proved for writable tokens only: a URL token, a bad URL, a range of code points, a unit or an unrestricted hash that needs an escape are written and guarded, with no theorem; the law is about `tokenize` and not `tokenizeText`: that preprocessing leaves the writer's text as it is is not proved; nothing says that a comment is needed where the writer puts one: only guards show a pair misread without it; the search for the digits of a fraction is bounded by the size of the denominator, and that it finds every decimal value is not proved: the test `Writable` checks its result, so the theorem does not rest on it. Discharged: theorems `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.tokenize_serialize`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.tokenize_serialize_eq`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.tokenize_text`, `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.stops_text` and `Whatwg.Css.Syntax.stops_comment`. |
| representation | `required-open` | The writer puts an empty comment between two tokens where the standard's table marks the pair, and in two more places that the table misses: the identifier `--` before `>`, and `<` before `!`.
